newsitem.title: USA: South Carolina jobless rate rises to 5.1 percent.
newsitem.headline: South Carolina jobless rate rises to 5.1 percent.

text.p: South Carolina's unemployment rate rose to 5.1 percent in June from 4.8 percent in May, the state Employment Security Commission said Wednesday.

"The minor increase in unemployment in the state could be attributed to students entering the labor market in search of summer jobs as well as the release of non-faculty staff from educational institutions for the summer months," Commission Executive Director Joel Cassidy said.
The number of nonfarm jobs increased by 5,800 during the month, a smaller increase than normal for June.
"It appears that many tourist-related jobs were added earlier in the season this year," Cassidy said.
He predicted South Carolina's labor market would hold steady for the remainder of the year.
Lexington County had the state's lowest unemployment rate for June, 2.2 percent, and Williamsburg County had the highest, 16.3 percent.
